# Sharp joint parity effects from finite-rate dephasing

Author: gb_finite_rate_genesis. Date: 2026-10-16. Status: internally derived; external correctness and historical priority UNKNOWN.

## 1. The source question and the new answer

`finite_rate_joint_syndrome_2026-10-15/joint/REPORT.md` explicitly leaves open whether the single-parity factor

    epsilon_i(T) = J_i^2 [ T/gamma_i
                        - (1-exp(-2 gamma_i T))/(2 gamma_i^2) ]

multiplies across simultaneous disjoint-parity interactions sharing an arbitrary finite bath. It proves the larger positive majorant B instead. Under its exact single-parity hypotheses, the sharp epsilon PRODUCT DOES hold. In fact an explicit latent-history bad effect, containing the endpoint event, has this bound. No physical measurements or new resources have to be added to the specified exact Lindblad evolution to prove the endpoint assertion.

The proof is an application of the previously supplied deletion-null instrument lemma to an exact Poisson-pinch representation. It does not prove that an unspecified physical detector realizes the stipulated generator.

## 2. Endpoint theorem

Let Z_1,...,Z_k be commuting Hermitian involutions on a finite joint memory-bath Hilbert space. A reference can be tensored throughout. Let

    d rho/dt = -i[H_0(t) + sum_i V_i(t), rho]
               + sum_i gamma_i(t) (Z_i rho Z_i-rho),       (1)

on a fixed deterministic interval [0,T]. Assume, almost everywhere:

    [H_0(t),Z_i]=0,
    {V_i(t),Z_i}=0,
    [V_i(t),Z_j]=0 for i != j,
    ||V_i(t)|| <= j_i(t),

where j_i is nonnegative integrable and gamma_i nonnegative integrable. All propagators exist. There is no bound on H_0, no commutation assumption on bath coefficients, and no bath reset. The initial joint state is supported in a specified joint Z sector s; let P_s denote its projector.

Define

    E_i = integral_0^T integral_0^T j_i(t) j_i(u)
            exp[-2 integral_min(t,u)^max(t,u) gamma_i(v) dv] dt du.  (2)

For any selected set S, let P_flip(S,s) project onto outputs whose selected parities all differ from s, with no restriction on the other parities. If Phi_T is the channel of (1), then

    P_s Phi_T^*(P_flip(S,s)) P_s
        <= product_(i in S) min(1,E_i) P_s.                 (3)

# Independent adversarial audit: Poisson full-pinch history effects and the source epsilon-product

Date: 2026-10-16. Author: assigned interface-audit worker. Status: independent analytic reconstruction under the exact hypotheses below; externally unreviewed. This proof was constructed from the parent-supplied statement before reading any other worker's candidate. No novelty, device, asymptotic-memory, or formal-certification claim follows.

## 1. Decisive result

The source `finite_rate_joint_syndrome_2026-10-15/joint/REPORT.md`, Outcome and final paragraph, explicitly leaves open the product of the one-parity factors

\[
 \epsilon_i(t)=\frac{J_i^2}{\gamma_i}
 \left[t-\frac{1-e^{-2\gamma_i t}}{2\gamma_i}\right].
\]

That product follows under the literal source one-parity-per-interaction hypotheses. An alternative positive Kraus representation of the SAME dephasing dynamics proves a stronger history event, and avoids the exponential inflation in its double-Dyson majorant. The source's existing majorant remains valid; this is an additional proof, not an inconsistency in it.

The mechanism also proves the parent-supplied full-group version: for independent continuous generators `lambda_i (D_Gi - Id)`, exact entering/exiting pinches, and clean sector-preserving backgrounds,

\[
 F_S^{\rm history}\le
 \left(\prod_{i\in S}p_i\right)I,
 \qquad
 p_i=\min\left\{1,\;\frac{2J_i^2}{\lambda_i}
 \left[\tau_i-\frac{1-e^{-\lambda_i\tau_i}}{\lambda_i}\right]\right\}.
 \tag{1}
\]

`History bad` means at least one syndrome change between ANY successive latent complete-pinch records within that parent, including the exact endpoints. It is stronger than final syndrome mismatch. The cut records are labels in a legitimate global Kraus representation, not promised controller outputs.

## 2. Exact source hypotheses and conclusion

The source statement in `independent/INDEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_SUBSET_PROOF.md`, Section 1 (A), is

\[
 [H_0(t),Z_i]=0,\quad \{V_i(t),Z_i\}=0,\quad
 [V_i(t),Z_j]=0\ (j\ne i),\quad \|V_i(t)\|\le J_i,
 \tag{2}
\]

with commuting Hermitian involutions `Z_i`, independent exact dephasers `gamma_i(Ad Z_i - Id)`, and initial joint sector `Pi_s`. Time-dependent self-adjoint Hamiltonians and an arbitrary finite persistent bath/reference are allowed. The coefficients are the given Hamiltonian operators; they do not read a chosen latent unraveling's internal cut records
